description: Native Chrome and Safari production-editor drawing responsiveness and pixel-correctness validation after separating live stroke feedback from persisted raster work.

scope.coverage: A seven-case suite per browser, plus focused continuous-input, application DPR=1, and pointer-cancellation reruns. Focused runs overlap suite coverage; their case counts are not additional distinct features.
included: Native OCR recognition, selection and return to drawing

stressFixture.placement: Original-resolution source fitted into the smaller document

continuousInput.dispatch: Independent timer; no per-input canvas readback or wait for worker completion

method.pixelObserver: Each animation frame copies pending and near-future 1x1 display pixels into a private sparse staging canvas, then performs one readback. It timestamps first observed brush color, excluding probes known to be painted before dispatch. Normal probes use non-overlapping centers; stress probes use the lower advancing brush edge.
method.observerCaveat: Readback and observation add measured CPU cost and frame quantization. These are conservative canvas-pixel observation times, not hardware display/photon timestamps. Observer p95, maximum, total CPU and readback counts are retained in each continuous summary. They are not subtracted from reported latency.

sampleTimingEncoding.reference: Milliseconds from that continuous stream start; tuple index is the input-sample index
sampleTimingEncoding.summaryPrecision: Original recorded numeric precision is preserved

method.delayedPersistence: A test-only Worker wrapper delays each outgoing beginStroke, strokePoints and finishStroke RPC by 250 ms while preserving FIFO ordering. This simulates a backed-up persistence queue; it does not throttle the physical disk. delayMs records the requested global delay. Blank, eraser, reset, barriers and transformed cases additionally enforce a local minimum 250 ms delay where recorded.
method.foreground: Each case starts in a visible, focused window. Visibility/focus transitions are recorded. Losing foreground or input dispatch falling more than 1000 ms behind schedule invalidates timing results instead of counting as a drawing regression.
method.devicePixelRatio: Native runs report application DPR=2. DPR=1 runs override only configurable window.devicePixelRatio before the application bundle loads and record nativeDevicePixelRatio=2, requestedDevicePixelRatio=1 and whether the override succeeded. Physical display density and browser compositing scale do not change.
method.rapidStrokes: Twenty approximately 40 ms strokes with approximately 40 ms gaps, without waiting for persistence; all twenty are required to remain independently undoable.
method.pendingBarriers: After pointerup, wait one animation frame for React to publish current controls, verify saving/mutation work is still pending, then exercise size calculation, PNG Blob export, Undo/Redo, layer selection and zoom.
method.pointerCancellation: Focused blank-layer reruns dispatch pointercancel without client coordinates. Live and saved pixels must retain only the accepted prefix; authoritative native bounds exclude a spurious segment toward the default origin, and Undo/Redo preserve the result.
method.transformedClipping: A centered 300x200 source is scaled to 50% and rotated 30 degrees through the UI. A stroke crosses the source boundary; live, committed and exported pixels are checked inside and outside that boundary.
reproduce: Open the native browser window in the foreground and click Ready; use latencycheck=normal or stress, case=all or a focused case, optional delayms=250 and dpr=1.
method.baselineCaveat: Only the specifically identified Safari baseline met benchmark-validity conditions. The Chrome baseline is summary-only and explicitly invalid. No before/after ratio is asserted in this artifact.
method.editorChecksCaveat: The editor functional checks wait for settled state and establish eventual correctness. Responsiveness deadlines are established by the separate continuous-input pixel observer.

results.invalidReason: Input dispatch fell over 1000 ms behind schedule; rerun in a foreground native window before judging drawing latency.
results.errorSummary: Error: Input-to-visible p95 exceeded the drawing budget

chromeInvalidAuditOnly.interpretation: Invalid timing benchmark: the nominal five-second stream took 12.785 seconds and the sparse observer consumed 9.932 seconds of CPU. Retained for audit only; do not use its latency values for a before/after comparison or ratio.

manualNativeChecks.evidence: Direct native browser UI observations. No screenshots retained.
